_note: Original advanced concept questions for two pointers.

questions.title: Two-pointer purpose
questions.prompt: What is the main idea of a two-pointer solution?
questions.explanation: Two pointers work because each pointer move removes choices you no longer need.
choices: Move two indexes using a rule

questions.title: Sorted two-sum
questions.prompt: In a sorted list, the left+right sum is too small. Which pointer should move?
questions.explanation: Moving left rightward increases the sum because the list is sorted.
questions.code:
nums = [1, 2, 4, 7, 11]
target = 10
left value = 1
right value = 7
sum = 8

questions.title: Too-large sum
questions.prompt: In a sorted list, the left+right sum is too large. Which pointer should move?
questions.explanation: Moving right leftward lowers the sum because the right value gets smaller.
questions.code:
nums = [1, 2, 4, 7, 11]
target = 10
left value = 4
right value = 11
sum = 15

questions.title: Palindrome pointers
questions.explanation: The first check compares the outer characters before the pointers move inward.

questions.title: After finding a pair
questions.prompt: After finding one valid pair, why might code move both pointers?
questions.explanation: Both used values have already formed the current pair, so moving both looks for a new pair without repeating the same one.
questions.code:
nums = [1, 2, 4, 6, 8]
target = 10
left value = 2
right value = 8
sum = 10
choices: To search for another pair without reusing the same two values
Because the array is no longer sorted
Because left must always move twice

questions.title: When to stop
questions.prompt: Why do many two-pointer loops stop when `left >= right`?
questions.explanation: When the pointers meet or cross, there is no pair of two different positions left to check.
questions.code:
while left < right:
    # check a pair
choices: There is no two-position pair left

questions.title: Two-pointer pair search
questions.explanation: The search checks a pair, then moves exactly the pointer that the sum proves is safe to move.
lines: Set left to 0 and right to the last index.
While left is less than right, compute the pair sum.
If the sum equals target, return true.
If the sum is too small, move left rightward.
If the sum is too large, move right leftward.
Return false when the pointers cross.

questions.title: Pointer bug
questions.prompt: What is a common bug in two-pointer code?
questions.explanation: Every pointer move should be justified by what the current comparison tells you.
questions.code:
while left < right:
    # pointer moves should match what the comparison tells you
choices: Moving a pointer without a reason tied to the condition
